faq.q: What is the origin of Qaiser?
faq.a: Qaiser is associated with Arabic. Qaiser is Arabic قَيْصَر (Qayṣar), a borrowing of the title Caesar, meaning 'emperor'.
Yes — the underlying form قَيْصَر is Arabic.
Qaiser can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Qaiser should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Qayṣar is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Qaiser mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Qaiser is rendered قیصر and carries the sense قیصر، بادشاہ.

faq.q: What does Qaiser mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Qaiser is rendered قیصر and carries the sense قیصر، امپراتور.
A romanized syllable approximation is qai-ser. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Qaiser?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Qaiser, qaiser. Script forms are قَيْصَر, قیصر, क़ैसर.

faq.q: Is Qaiser a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
